# Manannán walks into a maritime, shipping & ocean industries firm

Somewhere right now, in a maritime, shipping & ocean industries office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Manannán**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Chariot on the Wave-Plain.** In Immram Brain, the Voyage of Bran, the god meets a mortal expedition on its own element.  Bran mac Febail had heard music behind him until he slept, and woke to find a silver branch with white blossoms at his hand; a strange woman sang to him of the Land of Women until he put to sea with three companies of nine.  Out on the ocean a chariot came toward the boat, and the charioteer hailed Bran across the water — it was Manannán mac Lir, driving over what Bran took for the sea and the god took for a flowery plain.

**The Silver Apples of the Land of Promise.** Echtra Cormaic maic Airt i Tír Tairngiri sends him into Tara itself.  A warrior appeared at Cormac mac Airt's court bearing a branch with three silver apples that played sweet music; for it the king gave, one by one, his wife and his son and his daughter — and then grieved.  A grey-haired man with a shining branch led him through a mist into the Land of Promise, where four palaces stood and a pig was roasted and renewed every night, and where an aged couple kept an ever-full cauldron: 'the world is a wave,' the old man told him, 'ebbing and flowing.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries

*Manannán mac Lir, son of the sea itself — Ireland’s great wave-lord, navigator, and keeper of the ocean road.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Cybersecurity & Digital Protection

*His Answerer opens every fortress and compels the truth; the skeleton key and the audit in one blade.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP

*The misty Otherworld; Celtic fantasy’s gateway.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services

*The féth fíada that veils the Otherworld; concealment as a divine craft.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Communication, Messaging & Logistics

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The Wave-sweeper answers its owner's thought and the horse runs the sea-road; passage between islands is his craft.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Manannán was always going to be re-derived wherever sea, otherworld, mist matters.

## Not the First Rebrand

Manannán's closest counterpart is the Welsh Manawydan fab Llŷr, the patient, just, sea-wise figure of the Second and Third Branches of the Mabinogi — husband of [[rhiannon|Rhiannon]], and the one lord in the Welsh tales who cannot be outwitted or outwaited.  Both names rest on a Common Celtic *Manaw-, and both bear the same patronymic: son of Lir, son of Llŷr, the Sea. The office is only the latest translation.
